questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Ive been to Colombia before and loved it. Wanted to improve my spanish as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great expirence. Uniandes is great at welcoming exchange students, Bogotá is amazing, and the people ive met I consider friends for life. Only downside would be that my classes definetly varied alot in quality, with some being great and others being pretty bad. But overall it was very interesting to experience a different type of university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy... A LOT of bureaucracy, documents to fill, immigration stuff... I felt like Uniandes did what they could to help, but UCPH is not the most responsive....

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived everything was smooth from Uniandes. I did the spanish summer course which was a great experience, and Anderson (a guy that works there) is a great help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Shout out to Anderson.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: LivinnX18 where I lived didnt have any sheets, pots or pans, so I had to spend a night in my apartment without anything... if you plan on staying there (or "The Spot" or "City U"), prepare to spend some money on everything from knives to trashcans. However, overall I was happy to live at LivinnX18 and would recommend it, although it is pretty expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Both cityU and the Spot are pretty bad, so dont go there... no windows, for example, and only one stovetop. But if you dont mind living with other people, the best option is to live at one of the "casas" in Candelaria, "Casa Verde," "Casa Blanca," "Casa del Sol," "La Quinta" are all cheap and good options. I stayed a few weeks in Casa Verde which was nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is difficult to find a nice and cheap apartment that you have to yourself, you have to do it through something like LivinnX, which is pretty expensive. The housing that Uniandes provides (CityU) is, as I said, bad.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many documents, deadlines, and confusion to be honest. Totally worth it, but it required a lot of work.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had a zoom meeting explaining everything, so that was nice. But the language test was ridicolous and didnt matter, and immigration sucked as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All that was needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted. Not all turned out great however.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just stick with it, and take it one thing at the time. At some point you will reach the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found that most of my teachers where welcoming and overbearing when it came to exchange students, and gave us a lot of slack in everything from paper-deadlines to attendance.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In Colombia it is normal to begin university when you are like 17-18. So classes for first year students are therefore not that high level, and I would recommend avoiding them. Maybe ask around for other students favourite teachers and classes, before picking.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of papers and assignements... like every week. Unlike UCPH - where you have 1 final exam that counts for your entire grade -, at Uniandes you have assignments, attendance, participation, and other stuff to determine your grade. But this is not as bad as it sounds, and you have plenty of freetime to do what you want. However, i Definetly prefer the danish way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Populism in Global Perspective. 
Naturaleza y Cultura. 
Introduction a la politica colombiana. 
Cine Colombiano.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Populism in Global Perspective, because of the teacher Luke Melchoire. He was great, and the class was very interesting. Any class he teaches im sure is great. Naturaleza y Cultura was also nice. The others, not so much. Especially Introduction a la politica colombiana... I would avoid anything Ingrid Ramirez teaches.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Buying apartment stuff. But Colombia is very cheap, so everything from food to phone data is very much bearable.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is less expensive than expected. Except housing, which was european prices. (Unless you go to Candelaria, which I would recommend).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: didnt join any, but they all seemed nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different clubs. Also "Hermanos sin fronteras" are a greeeaat help, and all of them very nice. If you are going to uniandes, they will be a life saver.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Salsa classes!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travelling. See the Amazon, see the coast, see the mountains. Such an amazing country. Good food in Bogotá is in Chapinero and Usaquén. If you can find a guide that lives there that you trust, go the Ciudad Bolivar. It is poor, but very charismatic and a huge experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Colombians are the friendliest most welcoming people in the world. Literally.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be yourself and dont feel pressured to do something you dont wanna do. You will definetly find likeminded people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe the food... It is allright, but im not a huge fan.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature and the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1: Save up. 2: Dont be paranoid (but dont be stupid either). 3: Buy an umbrella.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The trips i went on to the Amazon, San Andres, and Tayrona. The people I met at Uniandes. Learning spanish.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dont know... Maybe UCPH not wanting to preapprove the courses I wanted to take... But in Colombia life was great and easy. Do it!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Great experience, you wont regret doing it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
